messages:
alex_cheng: Hey team — customer AcmeCorp POC hitting two blockers: (1) their QSA asked for network/KMS diagrams and an encryption matrix, and (2) our demo is intermittently returning truncated JSON from function/tool calls. They want a commercial pricing ask for Dedicated if we can guarantee <100ms p95 and SOC2 in the contract. Can we triage?

emily_ruiz: Thanks Alex. Can you drop a minimal repro + logs? Is the truncation happening on short outputs or long ones? :thinking:

alex_cheng: repro attached (curl + sample prompt). Truncation seems correlated with streaming responses — sometimes the JSON stops mid-object. Log snippet below.

alex_cheng: ```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] request_id=req-0a1b2c status=200 model=rw-3b mode=jsonstream tokens=432
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] response_chunk="{\"result\": { \"items\": [\"a\", \"b\""
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] response_chunk=", \"c\"] } }"
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] connection_close client=acme-app code=499
```

priya_sinha: Looks like client-side connection close (499) — streaming may be cut by the client or a proxy. Do we have evidence of server-side hitting token limit or 429?

alex_cheng: We also see 429 spikes earlier in the trace from a burst of parallel requests. Example header: `Retry-After: 2` and `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`. But the timing doesn't perfectly align with every truncation.

sean_sales: On pricing — Acme asked if we can commit to dedicated pool + 20% discount for a 12mo commit. They'll sign if the security answers are complete. Carla, can you help with the QSA package?

carla_gomez: Yep. I have a draft network diagram and KMS notes. QSA also asked: "How is customer data separated from other tenants in Hosted?" We should recommend Dedicated for their compliance needs. I'll attach diagrams and a short FAQ.

emily_ruiz: For engineering side — two parallel asks: (A) immediate POC reliability fix, (B) longer-term guardrails for streaming+json toolcall outputs. Quick mitigation: fallback to non-streaming or add end-of-message sentinel + retry logic when client receives truncated JSON. Also can set `max_output_tokens` higher than anticipated to avoid hitting server-side truncation from token cap.

priya_sinha: Agreed. Also add `Content-Length`/keepalive checks between their proxy and client. On server side, we should verify no early close from our edge: eng-oncall-bot, can you grep for req-0a1b2c trace and confirm server closed connection?

eng-oncall-bot: Querying traces for request_id=req-0a1b2c...

eng-oncall-bot: Trace found: upstream runtime returned full payload and chunked transfer completed. Last event: client_connection_close at 2026-03-18T14:02:11Z. No server-side cutoff.

priya_sinha: That matches — truncation is client/proxy-initiated. Two action items: 1) recommend non-streaming or implement `json_mode: relaxed` for tolerant parsing; 2) ask client infra to increase timeout/keepalive and handle retries/backoff for 499s. I can draft a short note they can share with their infra team.

alex_cheng: Great. For the customer-facing workaround, can we provide a code snippet for robust parse with retry and merging partial chunks?

emily_ruiz: Yep, sending a tiny example.

emily_ruiz: ```javascript
// pseudo-code: collect streaming chunks, detect incomplete JSON, retry if connection truncated
let buf = ''
for await (chunk of stream) { buf += chunk }
try { const parsed = JSON.parse(buf) } catch (e) { if (e instanceof SyntaxError) { // possible truncation -> retry with backoff
  await retryFetchWithBackoff()
 } else { throw e } }
```

carla_gomez: For the QSA: I'll include KMS integrations (customer-managed keys on Dedicated and HSM notes), data residency statement, and a sample SOC2 scope. Also confirm we can add IP allowlists and VPC peering for Private.

sean_sales: Do we have an internal pricing playbook for 12mo Dedicated commits? I need a quick range to tell Acme tonight.

alex_cheng: @sean_sales, we can offer a baseline 15% commit discount, push to 20% for Exec approval if they meet usage thresholds. I'll loop in finance after we confirm security items.

priya_sinha: Back to technical POC: suggest they flip the demo to non-streaming for now. If they must stream, add a small post-processing step to append missing closing braces when we detect chunked cut (safe only for predictable outputs). Also recommend exponential backoff for 429 and 499 with jitter.

emily_ruiz: Also callout: when using function calling, prefer strict schema validation on the receiver side and tolerant parsing when reading model outputs. If their schema is large, the model might produce partial output; consider sending smaller tasks or using continuation tokens.

alex_cheng: OK plan: Carla will deliver QSA package by EOD tomorrow; Priya will draft infra note + backoff snippet; Emily will send parsing example + a non-streaming curl demo; I will reply to Acme with the 15% baseline offer and timeline. Anyone blocking?

carla_gomez: No blockers from security. I'll attach diagrams in the next message. :thumbsup:

priya_sinha: No blockers. I'll send infra note in ~2 hours.

emily_ruiz: sending curl non-streaming example now.

emily_ruiz: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-3b","prompt":"...","stream":false,"max_output_tokens":1024}'
```

alex_cheng: Thanks all — I'll update Acme and close the POC blocker thread once they confirm network tweaks + pricing OK.

sean_sales: Thanks — ping me when security package is uploaded and I6ll route the discount request to finance.

eng-oncall-bot: Notification: trace req-0a1b2c archived to ticket INF-4873.
